market_context: United States; whole raw potatoes in home storage
title: How long do potatoes last when stored properly?

seo.title: How long do potatoes last when stored properly?
seo.meta_description: At room temperature potatoes keep best quality for about a week; in a truly cool, dark, ventilated place around 45-50°F they can last several weeks. Commercial storage can extend that to months.
seo.search_intent: Give realistic potato storage times and explain the conditions that extend quality and the signs that mean a potato should be discarded.

excerpt: In a warm home kitchen, potatoes generally keep their best quality for about a week. In a dark, well-ventilated and genuinely cool place around 45-50°F (7-10°C), they can stay fresh for several weeks. Multi-month figures refer to controlled crop-storage conditions and should not be treated as a normal pantry promise.
content_html:
Saying potatoes “last for months” is not useful without describing the storage room. The same bag may sprout quickly beside a warm appliance and remain sound for weeks in a cool dark cellar. Temperature, light, ventilation and starting quality all change the clock.

One week and several weeks can both be right

NDSU Extension says potatoes retain their best quality for about one week at room temperature. At 45-50°F (7-10°C), they can stay fresh for several weeks.

Six- or nine-month storage figures come from crop-storage conditions with carefully managed cold temperature, high relative humidity, darkness and airflow. A typical kitchen cabinet does not reproduce that environment.

Darkness prevents more than cosmetic greening

Light turns exposed tissue green and can be associated with increased glycoalkaloids. Keep potatoes out of sunlight and bright countertops. A ventilated paper bag, box or dark basket is generally more useful than a sealed plastic bag that traps condensation.

Heat speeds sprouting and shriveling

A cupboard beside an oven, dishwasher or other heat source is a poor choice. Warmer potatoes respire faster, lose moisture and tend to sprout sooner.

High humidity can reduce shriveling in controlled storage, but wet surfaces and condensation favor rot. That is why extension guidance also advises against washing potatoes before long storage.

The calendar does not decide whether a potato is usable

A firm potato at ten days may be fine; a damaged potato can rot much sooner. Check for wet soft decay, mold, an abnormal odor and extensive greening.

Small sprouts can be removed from an otherwise firm, nongreen potato before cooking, but the sprouts themselves should not be eaten.

The home-kitchen rule

For supermarket potatoes, think about a week in a warm room and several weeks in a truly cool, dark location. Buying an amount you will actually use is often more realistic than trying to recreate commercial storage at home.

faq.question: How long do potatoes last at room temperature?
faq.answer: NDSU gives about one week for best quality at room temperature, although warmth and starting condition can shorten it.

faq.question: Can potatoes last several weeks?
faq.answer: Yes. Around 45-50°F in darkness with ventilation, extension guidance says they can remain fresh for several weeks.

faq.question: Should potatoes be washed before storage?
faq.answer: Not for long storage. Surface moisture can encourage spoilage; brush off dry soil and wash before cooking.
